_comment: Machine-evaluable encoding of matching rules R01-R30 (from the first notes) and R31-R38 (from research_notes/Emotion combination evidence map/, IDs as proposed in reports/Emotion combination evidence map.md). For R01-R30 the text fields (condition, recommended, avoid, rationale, citation, doi_or_url, evidence basis) are parsed from the notes table by the build script; this file adds the structured condition, class lists and explicit activity ids. A 'revised' block encodes the rule-review refinements (mixed_state_interventions.md '## Rule review'); the build uses it in place of the original lists and keeps the originals as original_*. R31-R38 carry their own text fields and 'citation_keys' (PMIDs or DOIs that must appear in the combination notes tables). 'Happy' in the notes = taxonomy id 'content'; 'excited' = 'energetic'. Thresholds 0.4 / 0.75 / 0.9 are uncalibrated engineering defaults.

class_definitions.SENSORY: cold water, warm shower, senses-based grounding
class_definitions.MOVE-MOD: self-paced brisk walk, run, sport, dancing
class_definitions.PLEASANT: planned enjoyable or mastery activity = behavioural activation

restless_fallback.note: The notes contain NO single-emotion rule for 'restless' and no evidence rows targeting it. This fallback is a judgement call made in this dataset build (high-arousal-negative quadrant principle plus R18's direction), marked extrapolated.

R01.app_note: Restricts the FIRST suggestion to these classes; cognitive or social options are offered as the follow-up.

R02.app_note: Adds REAPPRAISE and PLAN to whatever the emotion's own rule allows. 'Suppressing the feeling' has no activity id; never prompt it.

ask_user.question: Is this something you can do something about right now?

R04.app_note: At stressed >= 0.75 the single-emotion lookup still uses this rule, with R01 gating the first suggestion. Comfort eating and alcohol are never suggested.

R10.app_note: Defer PLAN to 'later, one small step'. Music should be calm.

revised.app_note: Detach from the stressor first (close work, mute notifications). Nap about 10 minutes if sleep-deprived, not 30. A short walk lifts energy; expect fatigue relief only from easy movement lasting more than 20 minutes. Offer one low-effort pleasant activity. Defer PLAN to 'later, one small step'. Music should be calm.

R10.revision_note: Detach first, then rest or breathing; 10-min nap if sleep-deprived (not 30); a short walk is for energy, fatigue relief needs easy movement for more than 20 min; add one low-effort pleasant activity because exhaustion erodes detachment unless pleasurable leisure is present.

ask_user.question: Is this something you can do something about right now?

revised.app_note: If the stress is about an upcoming evaluated task (exam, talk, interview), offer the 'this energy helps me' arousal reappraisal as an option.

R11.revision_note: Mindfulness helps stress more than anxiety (consistent with the rule); when the stress is about an upcoming evaluated task, offer arousal reappraisal.

R12.app_note: SOCIAL must be in a low-demand form (text a trusted person, co-walk). BREATHE first if intensity is high.

revised.app_note: SOCIAL in a low-demand form (text a trusted person before a call; empathic one-to-one contact). A low-exposure kind act is directly supported in socially anxious adults. Mindfulness should be acceptance-based, not monitoring only. BREATHE first if intensity is high.

R12.revision_note: Confirmed; add acceptance-based mindfulness, a low-exposure kind act and warm one-to-one contact (text before call).

R13.app_note: Sequence matters: calm first, then journalling or reappraisal, then talk to a supportive person.

revised.app_note: Sequence: calm the body, distract (something absorbing or funny), then reflect from a distance (use your name or 'you', ask why), then talk to a supportive person. Undirected expressive journalling is not offered.

R13.revision_note: Calm first, then distract, then self-distanced reflection (third person, 'why'), then talk to a supportive person; undirected expressive writing is dropped.

R14.app_note: Keep movement easy or playful. Do not prompt sending messages while angry.

revised.app_note: Keep movement easy and physically away from the trigger ('step away from the screen first'): moderate exercise done while viewing upsetting images raised anger. Distraction over rumination. Nature is the weakest-supported option for the anger part. Do not prompt sending messages while angry.

R14.revision_note: Confirmed; keep movement easy and away from the provoking input, use distraction over rumination, and treat nature as weak for the anger part.

R15.app_note: Very small step (5-10 min); low-effort social form (voice note); REST if sleep-deprived. max_typical_duration_min = 20 is this build's encoding of 'very small step'.

revised.app_note: Very small step (5-10 min). Rest is a first-line option. A short walk tends to lift energy, but fatigue relief needs easy movement for more than 20 minutes; keep the copy modest. Low-effort social form (voice note). max_typical_duration_min = 20 is this build's encoding of 'very small step'.

R15.revision_note: Rest is promoted to a first-line option (rest matched exercise on negative mood in depression); a walk is for energy; keep fatigue claims modest.

revised.app_note: Reach out to one specific person (text before call). Prefer active or shared music over solitary sad-music loops. Nostalgia (positive_reminiscence) is a follow-up the user opts into, framed toward connection, not loss. Never suggest getting a pet. Say that loneliness eases with repeated contact; one message is a start.

R16.revision_note: Confirmed; warm one-to-one contact is directly supported; prefer active or shared music; nostalgia only as an opt-in framed toward connection; never suggest getting a pet.

revised.app_note: Movement, yoga or mindfulness first; PLEASANT/behavioural activation after them. PMR alone is a weak match for the sad part. Single-session anxiety effects are small. Reflection, if any, should be self-distanced.

R17.revision_note: Lead with movement, yoga or mindfulness, which move both outcomes; rank PLEASANT/behavioural activation after them (digital BA lowered depression, not anxiety).

R18.app_note: Sitting meditation should not be the first option.

R19.app_note: Prefer one activity that supplies both engagement and connection (game with a friend, class, club).

R20.app_note: Check whether the 'boredom' is fatigue: rest first, then light novelty. extra_activity_ids stand for the notes' 'easy creative task'.

revised.app_note: Check whether the 'boredom' is fatigue: rest first (a 10-minute nap, not 30), then light novelty. extra_activity_ids stand for the notes' 'easy creative task'.

R20.revision_note: Nap length: a 10-min nap is most recuperative; 30 min causes sleep inertia.

R21.app_note: Body scan / muscle relaxation; wind-down routine; calm music. PLAN is avoided here because the notes say no problem-solving in bed.

ask_user.question: Is this something you can do something about right now?

revised.app_note: Slow breathing or mindfulness, or a self-paced/green walk, then a small pleasant step; dance if energy allows.

R22.revision_note: Confirmed (strongest pair): low-arousal options (slow breathing, mindfulness) did as well as the hormetic arms in mixed-state trials, so they join walking as first options.

R23.app_note: MOVE-LOW here stands for the notes' 'co-walk' (walk with someone).

R24.app_note: Nothing to avoid; do not push calming activities.

R25.app_note: extra_activity_ids stand for the notes' 'gentle creative hobby'. Also used as the default when no emotion is active (neutral).

R27.app_note: Mixed valence: show both labels, never force a single one. extra_activity_ids stand for 'journalling / naming both feelings'. A specific pair rule (e.g. R26) outranks this one.

revised.app_note: Mixed valence: show both labels, never force a single one, use acceptance framing ('both can be true') and keep the positive part. Naming both feelings has only weak support. For excited + anxious with an upcoming task, offer 'I'm excited' reappraisal first and slow breathing as the alternative; without a task, calming options remain reasonable. Reminiscence should be framed toward connection. A specific pair rule (e.g. R26) outranks this one.

R27.revision_note: Keep 'don't suppress either feeling' and acceptance framing; 'name both feelings' has only weak support; for excited + anxious before a task, lead with 'I'm excited' arousal reappraisal, breathing as the alternative (contradicts BREATHE-first).

R28.app_note: Iso principle: start with a track matching the current mood, move toward the target mood over 2-3 tracks; let the user choose the tracks.

R29.app_note: Rank inside the allowed classes by likes/hobbies and past helpfulness; filter dislikes; show 2-3 choices; rotate for variety. A preference never overrides a rule's avoid list.

R30.app_note: Skip the activity list; show the supportive message and localised crisis resources (see safety.json). The grounding exercise is optional. The 0.9 threshold is an uncalibrated precaution, not a screening tool.

text.label: Tense distress cluster
text.condition_text: Three or more of stressed, anxious, angry, sad >= moderate
text.recommended_text: One shared-mechanism activity (slow breathing, green walk, yoga) before any component-specific step
text.avoid_text: Rumination; stacking several cognitive tasks; PMR alone if sad is high; venting; exercising amid the trigger
text.rationale: Stressed, frustrated, worried, angry and sad load on one day-level factor (Lucas 2018) and DASS stress, anxiety and depression correlate .77-.83. Mixed-state breathing and PMR trials and same-sample forest and yoga data improved several of these together.

R31.evidence_basis_text: Same-sample + mixed-state trials; moderate for programmes, extrapolated for a 5-min session (reports/Emotion combination evidence map.md)

deprioritise_when.reason: PMR improved stress and anxiety but not depression in two of four PMR studies

R31.app_note: Lead with one activity that works on shared distress, then add one component-specific step (a small pleasant activity if sad is high). If angry is active, keep movement easy and away from the trigger.

text.label: Sad + anxious + tired
text.condition_text: sad, anxious and tired all >= moderate
text.recommended_text: Rest or breathing, then an easy outdoor walk; a 10-min nap if sleep-deprived
text.avoid_text: Hard or maximal exercise; demanding plans; 30-min naps
text.rationale: Fatigue was endorsed by 94.2% of comorbid GAD+MDD cases. In depression, quiet rest matched exercise on every negative POMS subscale, maximal walking raised fatigue, and forest walks, a single Hatha yoga session, tele-PMR and a nap improved anxiety, depression and fatigue in the same samples.

R32.evidence_basis_text: Extrapolated from R15/R17/R21 plus nap and rest data; upgraded where same-sample rows exist
R32.app_note: Rest is evidence-based here, not a fallback. Promise calmer, not less tired, from a short walk.

text.label: Sad + anxious + angry
text.condition_text: sad, anxious and angry all >= moderate
text.recommended_text: Treat as R13: arousal-lowering activity or distraction first, then self-distanced reflection
text.avoid_text: Venting; exercise amid the trigger; undirected expressive writing; rumination
text.rationale: Irritability was endorsed by 84.5% of comorbid GAD+MDD cases and 28.7% of highly lonely adults screened positive for depression, anxiety and anger together. Arousal-decreasing activities reduce anger; rumination raises aggression; self-distancing lowered negative affect after anger recall and in depression; exercise amid aversive input raised anger.

R33.evidence_basis_text: Extrapolated; the anger component is the best tested
R33.app_note: Calm the body or distract first; reflect from a distance only afterwards. Step away from the trigger before any movement.

text.label: Lonely + sad + anxious
text.condition_text: lonely, sad and anxious all >= moderate
text.recommended_text: Low-demand warm contact (text first) or a kind act; acceptance framing; raise the sensitivity of the R30 safety check
text.avoid_text: Group or high-stakes social tasks; nostalgia by default; passive scrolling; getting a pet
text.rationale: 48.1% of highly lonely adults screened positive for both depression and anxiety. Empathy-focused calls reduced loneliness, depression and anxiety together; kind acts raised PA and lowered avoidance in socially anxious adults; acceptance-based mindfulness reduced loneliness; addressing social cognition is the most effective loneliness strategy.

R34.evidence_basis_text: Direct (Kahlon; Alden & Trew) for the programme components
R34.app_note: Text a trusted person before suggesting a call; offer empathy_phone_call as a plan-ahead option. Use acceptance framing. Nostalgia only if the user opts in, framed toward connection. This profile marks a high-load group: apply the R30 persistence check with extra care.

text.label: Lonely + bored + sad (disconnected)
text.condition_text: lonely, bored and sad all >= moderate
text.recommended_text: A shared or group activity, then a kind act or a matched challenge
text.avoid_text: Passive scrolling; open 'sit and reflect'; flag persistent bored + sad to R30
text.rationale: Lonely and bored form their own day-level factor with sad cross-loading (Lucas 2018); boredom correlates .60 with depression and .53 with loneliness. Six months of community choir improved loneliness and interest in life together; boredom and sadness frequency are the emotions most tied to depression in daily diaries; reflective thinking is enjoyable only on meaningful and positive topics.

R35.evidence_basis_text: Same-sample (choir, programme) + diary association; momentary use extrapolated
R35.app_note: Prefer one activity that supplies both engagement and connection (a game with a friend, a class). If reflection is offered, use a guided positive-and-meaningful prompt. Persistent bored + sad across check-ins should feed the R30 persistence signal.

text.label: Stressed + tired + sad (burnout-like)
text.condition_text: stressed, tired and sad all >= moderate
text.recommended_text: Detach and rest, then low-effort pleasant leisure
text.rationale: Burnout correlates .52 with depression. Detachment interventions and pleasurable leisure protect recovery from exhaustion; PMR with music lowered stress and fatigue in stressed, fatigued nurses; quiet rest matched exercise on negative mood in depression.

R36.app_note: Detach first (close work, mute notifications). Planning, if any, is one small step for later.

text.label: Anxious + restless
text.recommended_text: Slow breathing, then rhythmic easy movement (walk, gentle yoga)
text.avoid_text: Sitting meditation as the only or first option; caffeine
text.rationale: Psychomotor agitation was endorsed by 91.6% of GAD cases. Music interventions reduced psychological stress outcomes that the authors frame as including restlessness. No study in the notes used restlessness as an outcome; the activity choice is extrapolated from R05 and the restless fallback.

R37.app_note: Offer movement early; sitting still should not be the only option.

text.label: Positive + negative blend
text.condition_text: any positive class and any negative class >= moderate
text.recommended_text: Keep the positive: acceptance framing plus an activity that uses it (savour, share, easy movement)
text.avoid_text: Activities aimed at removing the positive part
text.rationale: About a third of sampled moments are mixed. Frequent mixed emotions predict better health, acceptance of mental experiences predicts lower negative affect under stress, and contentment speeds recovery from anxious arousal.

R38.app_note: Applied with R27 (or a mixed-valence pair rule such as R26): its classes are appended after the governing rule's classes.

_matrix_comment: The matrix now covers all 66 pairs of the 12 classes; matrix_extra_pairs is kept empty for backward compatibility.
